tool.name: AdapterRemoval: remove adapter sequences
tool.command:
#if $input_type_cond.input_type in ['single', 'pair', 'interleaved']: #set read1 = $input_type_cond.read1 #if $input_type_cond.input_type == 'pair': #set read2 = $input_type_cond.read2 #end if #else: #set read1 = $input_type_cond.reads_collection['forward'] #set read2 = $input_type_cond.reads_collection['reverse'] #end if
#set read1_identifier = 'read1' + $read1.ext ln -s '${read1}' '${read1_identifier}' &&
#if $input_type_cond.input_type in ["pair", "paired"]: #set read2_identifier = 'read2' + $read2.ext ln -s '${read2}' '${read2_identifier}' && #end if
adapterremoval3 --in-file1 '${read1_identifier}' #if $input_type_cond.input_type in ['pair', 'paired']: --in-file2 '${read2_identifier}' #end if #if str($input_type_cond.input_type) == 'interleaved': --interleaved-input #end if #if $input_type_cond.input_type in ['pair', 'paired', 'interleaved'] and str($input_type_cond.interleaved_output) == 'yes': --interleaved-output #end if
--threads "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-8}" --out-format fastq.gz
###### FASTQ Options --quality-format '33' $fastq_options.convert_uracils $fastq_options.mask_degenerate_bases
###### Adapter Selection --adapter-selection '$adapter_cond.adapter_selection' #if str($adapter_cond.adapter_selection) == 'manual': --adapter1 '$adapter_cond.adapter1' --adapter2 '$adapter_cond.adapter2' #if $adapter_cond.adapter_table: --adapter-table '$adapter_cond.adapter_table' #end if #end if
###### Read Alignment Options #if str($alignment_options.min_overlap): --min-overlap $alignment_options.min_overlap #end if --mismatch-rate $alignment_options.mismatch_rate --shift $alignment_options.shift
###### FASTQ Merging Options (paired-end input only) #if $input_type_cond.input_type in ['pair', 'paired', 'interleaved'] and str($fastq_merging_options.merge) != '': $fastq_merging_options.merge --merge-threshold $fastq_merging_options.merge_threshold --merge-strategy '$fastq_merging_options.merge_strategy' --merge-quality-max $fastq_merging_options.merge_quality_max #end if
###### FASTQ Trimming Options #if str($fastq_trimming_options.pre_trim3p_cond.trim_param) == 'yes': --pre-trim3p $fastq_trimming_options.pre_trim3p_cond.trim_mate1 $fastq_trimming_options.pre_trim3p_cond.trim_mate2 #end if #if str($fastq_trimming_options.post_trim5p_cond.trim_param) == 'yes': --post-trim5p $fastq_trimming_options.post_trim5p_cond.trim_mate1 $fastq_trimming_options.post_trim5p_cond.trim_mate2 #end if #if str($fastq_trimming_options.post_trim3p_cond.trim_param) == 'yes': --post-trim3p $fastq_trimming_options.post_trim3p_cond.trim_mate1 $fastq_trimming_options.post_trim3p_cond.trim_mate2 #end if --quality-trimming '$fastq_trimming_options.quality_trimming_cond.quality_trimming' #if str($fastq_trimming_options.quality_trimming_cond.quality_trimming) == 'mott': --trim-mott-rate $fastq_trimming_options.quality_trimming_cond.trim_mott_rate #else if str($fastq_trimming_options.quality_trimming_cond.quality_trimming) == 'window': --trim-windows $fastq_trimming_options.quality_trimming_cond.trim_windows --trim-min-quality $fastq_trimming_options.quality_trimming_cond.trim_min_quality #else if str($fastq_trimming_options.quality_trimming_cond.quality_trimming) == 'per-base': --trim-min-quality $fastq_trimming_options.quality_trimming_cond.trim_min_quality #end if $fastq_trimming_options.preserve5p
###### Poly-X Trimming Options #if str($polyx_options.pre_trim_polyx_cond.mode) == 'all': --pre-trim-polyx #else if str($polyx_options.pre_trim_polyx_cond.mode) == 'custom': --pre-trim-polyx #echo ' '.join(str($polyx_options.pre_trim_polyx_cond.nucleotides).split(','))# #else: --pre-trim-polyx '$polyx_options.pre_trim_polyx_cond.mode' #end if #if str($polyx_options.post_trim_polyx_cond.mode) == 'all': --post-trim-polyx #else if str($polyx_options.post_trim_polyx_cond.mode) == 'custom': --post-trim-polyx #echo ' '.join(str($polyx_options.post_trim_polyx_cond.nucleotides).split(','))# #else: --post-trim-polyx '$polyx_options.post_trim_polyx_cond.mode' #end if --trim-polyx-threshold $polyx_options.trim_polyx_threshold
###### Filtering Options #if str($filtering_options.max_ns): --max-ns $filtering_options.max_ns #end if --max-ns-fraction $filtering_options.max_ns_fraction --min-length $filtering_options.min_length #if str($filtering_options.max_length): --max-length $filtering_options.max_length #end if #if str($filtering_options.min_mean_quality): --min-mean-quality $filtering_options.min_mean_quality #end if #if str($filtering_options.min_complexity): --min-complexity $filtering_options.min_complexity #end if
###### Reports --out-json '$output_json' --out-html '$output_html' $report_only
###### Read outputs (not produced when only a report is requested) #if not str($report_only): #if str($input_type_cond.input_type) == 'single': --out-file1 '$output_truncated' #else: #if str($input_type_cond.interleaved_output) == 'no': --out-file1 '$output_forward_truncated' --out-file2 '$output_reverse_truncated' #else: --out-file1 '$output_interleaved_truncated' #end if #end if #if 'output_singleton' in $output_select: --out-singleton '$output_singleton_truncated' #end if #if 'output_merged' in $output_select and $input_type_cond.input_type in ['pair', 'paired', 'interleaved'] and str($fastq_merging_options.merge) != '': --out-merged '$output_merged' #end if #if 'output_discarded' in $output_select: --out-discarded '$output_discarded' #end if #end if

tool.help:
**What it does**
Searches for and removes remnant adapter sequences, poly-X tails and low quality bases from high-throughput sequencing (HTS) data. This tool can analyze both single-end and paired-end data and can be used to merge overlapping paired-end reads into longer consensus sequences. Adapter sequences are determined automatically from the input data by default.
The following outputs, some of which are optional or are only produced under certain scenarios, are produced.
* **HTML report** - Human readable report covering the input data, trimming, merging and filtering statistics. * **JSON report** - The same statistics in a machine readable form, suitable for downstream parsing (for example by MultiQC). * **truncated** - File containing trimmed single-end reads. * **forward truncated** - File containing trimmed mate 1 reads. * **reverse truncated** - File containing trimmed mate 2 reads. * **interleaved truncated** - File containing trimmed mate 1 and mate 2 reads written one pair after the other. * **singleton truncated** - File containing trimmed paired reads for which the mate has been discarded. * **merged** - If read merging is enabled, contains overlapping mate-pairs which have been merged into a single read. * **discarded** - File containing reads discarded by the filtering options.
Trimmed reads are written as gzip compressed FASTQ (``fastqsanger.gz``).
-----
**Adapter Selection**
* **Auto** - AdapterRemoval attempts to determine the adapter sequences from the input data itself. This is the default and is recommended for most data. * **Manual** - The adapter sequences given below are used. For a detailed description of how to provide the appropriate adapter sequences, see the "Adapters" section of the online documentation. A tabular file of adapter pairs may be supplied instead, in which case the best aligning adapter pair is selected for each read (pair); the first two columns of each line must correspond to the values passed to --adapter1 and --adapter2, only column one is required in single-end mode, and lines starting with # are ignored. * **Undefined** - Adapters are trimmed based on overlap analysis between mates (paired-end data) and/or 5' barcodes. * **None** - The data is assumed to contain no adapter sequences.
-----
**Read Alignment Options**
* **Minimum number of overlapping bases required for an alignment to be considered valid** - Reads are only trimmed if the overlap between the read and the adapter is at least this many bases long, not counting ambiguous nucleotides (N). Leaving this empty uses the AdapterRemoval defaults, which are 1 in single-end mode and the merge threshold in paired-end mode. * **Maximum error rate allowed when aligning reads and/or adapters** - The allowed fraction of mismatches in the aligned region. * **Consider alignments where up to this number of nucleotides are missing from the 5' termini** - To allow for missing bases in the 5' end of the read, the program can let the alignment slip this many bases in the 5' end.
-----
**FASTQ Merging Options**
Paired-end only. When merging is enabled, read pairs overlapping by at least the merge threshold are merged into a single consensus sequence written to the **merged** output. Two strategies are available for recalculating the quality scores of merged bases: **maximum** uses Q=max(Q1,Q2) for matching bases, while **additive** uses Q=Q1+Q2, capped at the maximum Phred score. Both strategies use Q=abs(Q1-Q2) for mismatches and pick the highest quality base, unless the qualities are identical, in which case an 'N' is used.
-----
**FASTQ Trimming Options**
* **Fixed trimming** - Reads may be trimmed by a fixed amount at the 3' before adapter trimming, and at the 5' and/or 3' after adapter trimming but before quality based trimming. Specify separate values for mate 1 and mate 2 reads; the mate 2 value is ignored for single-end input. Note that post-trimming of the 5' trims both ends of merged reads, as both ends represent the 5' of a read. * **Strategy for trimming low quality bases** - Four strategies are available:
1. **Mott** - the modified Mott's algorithm, controlled by an error rate threshold. This is the default. 2. **Window** - window based trimming inspired by sickle, see below. 3. **Per-base** - individual bases below the minimum quality are trimmed. 4. **None** - no trimming of low quality bases.
* **Window based quality trimming** - If the window size is greater than or equal to 1, that number is used as the window size for all reads. If it is greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1, then that number is multiplied by the length of individual reads to determine the window size. If the window length is zero or is greater than the current read length, then the read length is used instead. Reads are trimmed as follows for a given window size:
1. The new 5' is determined by locating the first window where both the average quality and the quality of the first base in the window is greater than the minimum quality. 2. The new 3' is located by sliding the first window right, until the average quality becomes less than or equal to the minimum quality. The new 3' is placed at the last base in that window where the quality is greater than or equal to the minimum quality. 3. If no 5' position could be determined, the read is discarded.
-----
**Poly-X Trimming Options**
Poly-X tails may be trimmed both before read alignment and adapter trimming, and afterwards but before quality trimming. By default, pre-trimming is set to **auto**, which trims poly-G tails from data produced by known 2-colour systems, and post-trimming is disabled. Merged reads are not affected by post-trimming, as both of their ends are 5'. Only tails at least as long as the poly-X threshold are trimmed.
-----
**Filtering Options**
Reads are discarded after trimming if they contain too many ambiguous bases (in absolute terms and/or as a fraction of the read length), are shorter or longer than the given length limits, have a mean Phred quality below the given minimum, or have a complexity score below the given minimum. Complexity is measured as the fraction of positions that differ from the previous position; a suggested value is 0.3.
